title: Kia Seltos 2026: Which Engine and Variant to Buy
description: Kia Seltos buyer’s brief, updated November 2026: ₹11.25 lakh start, turbo-petrol now DCT-only, five-star Bharat NCAP. Specification-led, not a road test.

hero.alt: Green second-generation Kia Seltos parked outside a modern building at sunset, with the headline Kia Seltos, 2026 Buying Review
hero.caption: AI illustration: FlamingPiston

standfirst: Since its launch, the second-generation Seltos has gained a top GTX(O) trim, had a price rise and, this week, lost its turbo-petrol iMT. This review is updated for all three.
note: This review uses Kia India’s published specifications and prices, the Bharat NCAP report and other publications’ drives, not our own test. Prices and specifications were checked on 21 November 2026. See our Review Methodology for how we separate editorial assessment from measured testing.
quickVerdict: The Seltos is one of the safest, most complete family SUVs you can buy at this price, and its best version is not the most expensive one. Pick the engine first, then stop at HTK(O) or HTX unless you specifically want the driver-assistance pack. The one thing to watch: with the iMT gone, the turbo-petrol now starts well into the middle of the range.

sections.heading: Exterior Design
sections.body:
The new Seltos moves to Kia’s K3 platform and has grown to match. It is 4,460 mm long, 1,830 mm wide and has a 2,690 mm wheelbase. Autocar India notes that is 95 mm longer than before, with an 80 mm longer wheelbase, which makes it the longest car in its class. The extra size helps the cabin. It also means a bigger footprint in a city parking space.

The styling is loud. Tall LED daytime running lights wrap up over the bonnet, square headlamps sit in a wide gloss-black grille, and the rear has vertical tail-lamps joined by a light bar. Higher trims get 18-inch alloys, and the X-Line pack adds black wheels and darker trim. It is a design you will either like at first sight or not at all.

image.alt: 2026 Kia Seltos in a dark finish parked at dusk, front three-quarter view showing the tall LED daytime running lights and grille
image.caption: Image: Kia India

sections.heading: Interior Design & Practicality
sections.body:
The cabin is a strong point. Autocar India rated the fit and finish very good. It also liked that Kia kept physical toggles for temperature and fan speed, although the 5-inch climate screen sits behind the steering wheel rim. Rear-seat legroom is generous enough for six-footers, by the same account, with headroom that is only just adequate for them and a seat base that is short for tall passengers.

The boot holds a claimed 447 litres (VDA method), with a full-size spare under the floor. The Seltos is strictly a five-seater. If you need a third row, it is the wrong car.

image.alt: 2026 Kia Seltos dashboard with the 12.3-inch touchscreen, digital instrument cluster and two-spoke steering wheel
image.caption: Image: Kia India

sections.heading: Features & Safety
sections.body:
Every Seltos gets six airbags, electronic stability control, hill-start assist, downhill brake control, disc brakes on all four wheels, tyre-pressure monitoring, ISOFIX mounts and three-point belts with reminders for every seat. Kia calls this its 24-item standard safety pack.

The useful features arrive in steps. The HTK(O) adds the dual-pane panoramic sunroof, wireless charging and front parking sensors, plus ventilated front seats on automatics. The HTX brings the 12.3-inch touchscreen, Bose audio, dual-zone climate control and ventilated seats on every gearbox. The (A) trims add the Trinity screen panel, a 360-degree camera and Level 2 driver assistance with 21 functions. The GTX(O) goes to 28 functions and adds a head-up display, digital key, dashcam and air purifier. Rear ventilated seats are not offered on any trim.

image.alt: Cutaway side view of the 2026 Kia Seltos showing its front, side and curtain airbags deployed
image.caption: Image: Kia India

sections.heading: Mileage, Engine & Performance
sections.body:
There are three 1.5-litre engines: a naturally aspirated petrol, a turbo-petrol and a diesel. They carry over from the first-generation car. Kia quotes outputs in kW; the PS figures below are our conversions.

{{table:engines}}

Autocar India found the turbo-petrol smooth and strong, though its dual-clutch gearbox can fumble at crawling speeds. CarWale called it one of the most competent powertrains in the segment. The diesel is refined but, in Autocar India’s view, lacks punch, and its automatic shifts slowly. With the iMT gone, the turbo-petrol is now automatic-only and starts higher up the range.

{{table:mileage}}

These are the ARAI-certified figures reported by Rushlane and 91Wheels in April 2026. Kia does not publish them on its own pages. ARAI tests run in controlled conditions, so expect lower figures in traffic. The diesel manual remains the choice for high annual mileage.

sections.heading: Tech & Safety Deep-Dive
sections.body:
This section draws on the published Bharat NCAP report and other publications’ drives, not our own, in line with our Review Methodology. The Seltos earned five stars from Bharat NCAP in March 2026: 31.70 out of 32 for adult protection and 45.00 out of 49 for child protection. The frontal offset test scored 15.70 out of 16 and the side barrier test a full 16, and the side pole test was rated OK. Bharat NCAP tested the HTE(O) and GTX diesel automatics. The rating is listed as a base rating that applies to the variants in its annexure. When the results came out, Kia said the adult score was the highest yet for a combustion-engined car in the programme.

The driver-assistance suite is standard from HTX(A) upward. Autocar India found the lane-departure correction natural but the lane-centring busy on unevenly marked roads. Treat it as an aid on good highways, not a reason to pay for a higher trim.

Big cabin and a 447-litre boot, offset by a larger parking footprint.
The middle trims make sense; higher prices and a dearer turbo entry hurt the rest.

verdict.body: The second-generation Seltos does not reinvent the formula, and it does not need to. It is bigger inside, rides more comfortably according to the people who have driven it, and backs up its safety claims with one of the best Bharat NCAP results so far. The risk is the trim ladder. Each step adds something attractive, and it is easy to spend ₹5 lakh more than you planned. Choose the engine first: petrol IVT for city driving, turbo-petrol DCT if you enjoy driving, diesel for long distances. Then make each step up beyond HTK(O) earn its place.

no: City drivers who need a smaller footprint for tight parking
Anyone who wanted an affordable turbo-petrol with a clutchless manual

faqs.q: What is the price of the 2026 Kia Seltos?
faqs.a: Kia India lists trim-entry prices from ₹11,24,900 (HTE) to ₹21,56,900 (GTX(O) and X-Line(O)), ex-showroom. Diesel-automatic versions of the top trims cost more.

faqs.q: Is the Kia Seltos turbo-petrol still available with an iMT?
faqs.a: No. CarWale reported on 20 November 2026 that the iMT versions have been dropped, and Kia’s current brochure lists the turbo-petrol with the 7-speed DCT only. Kia has not made an announcement.

faqs.q: What is the Seltos Bharat NCAP rating?
faqs.a: Five stars for both adult and child protection, with 31.70 out of 32 and 45.00 out of 49, published in March 2026.

faqs.q: What mileage does the Seltos give?
faqs.a: ARAI-certified figures are 16.5 kmpl for the 1.5 petrol, 17.5 kmpl for the turbo-petrol DCT, 19.4 kmpl for the diesel manual and 17.8 kmpl for the diesel automatic. Expect less in daily driving.

faqs.q: Which Seltos variant has the panoramic sunroof?
faqs.a: The dual-pane panoramic sunroof starts from the HTK(O) trim.

faqs.q: Is the Kia Seltos a seven-seater?
faqs.a: No. It is a five-seater with a claimed 447-litre boot.
